Here the article IS CC BY 4.0 (Ubiquity Press), but the article body does NOT print the author list -- it says only "The list is given in Appendix A" (p. 4) and "The revised version is shown in Appendix B" (p. 9). Both candidate sources for the wording are therefore NC. This is the chinvararak_2021_ecr shape (only publication of the wording is NC = a source-level restriction), not the cucchi_2018_tas20 / conspiracy_asd shape (wording published by a CC BY deposit, instrument-level NC recorded as wording_rights=NC). ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK (Step 5b, 2026-09-04) -- the round's sentinel claim about resp=0 is PARTLY CORRECTED. The agent reported that resp=0 is an unstripped not-applicable code, on the basis that 'four person-game rows have all 12 items = 0 with playing_match = 3 (niet spelen)'. Re-reading the PLOS S3 .sav directly: only TWO rows have all 12 justice items = 0 (both playing_match=3), and only FIVE have all 4 decisionjustification items = 0 (2 playing_match=3, 1 playing_match=0, 2 NA). The zeros are overwhelmingly PARTIAL, not row-wise: of the 21 rows carrying any zero in the justice block, 19 have some-but-not-all zeros (74 zero cells total), and those rows split across playing_match 1/2/3 as 9/4/8 -- close to the overall 387/161/113 distribution, i.e. carrying a zero is NOT associated with not having played. The decisionjustification block has 24 zero cells over 9 rows (4 partial). So the person-level 'did not play' explanation is NOT supported. What survives, and is solid: resp=0 lies outside the 1-5 scale the paper states, it is rare (5-8 occurrences per item), and it is scattered singly within otherwise-normal response vectors -- which looks like a per-item no-answer/skip code rather than a scale point. Either way option_text is correctly blank on every row. Worth a GitHub issue against data/debacker_2018_coaching_justice.py, which drops only NaN; but file it as 'out-of-range 0 of unknown meaning', not as the not-applicable finding.
